author: LCM-Redaktion
title: Die Bedingungen des Friedens – Eine Analyse der Kommunistischen Partei des Sudan zur Zukunft des Landes
content:
Der seit April 2023 andauernde Krieg im Sudan hat nicht nur eine der schwersten humanitären Krisen der Gegenwart ausgelöst, sondern auch eine grundlegende Debatte über die Ursachen der politischen Instabilität und die Zukunft des sudanesischen Staates entfacht. Während zahlreiche regionale und internationale Vermittlungsinitiativen auf eine Beendigung der Kampfhandlungen und die Wiederaufnahme eines politischen Übergangsprozesses abzielen, bestehen innerhalb der sudanesischen politischen Landschaft erhebliche Unterschiede hinsichtlich der Bewertung dieser Ansätze und der Voraussetzungen für einen nachhaltigen Frieden.


Vor diesem Hintergrund kommt den Stellungnahmen der sudanesischen politischen Parteien besondere Bedeutung zu. Sie spiegeln unterschiedliche Interpretationen der Ursachen des Krieges, der Rolle staatlicher und gesellschaftlicher Akteure sowie der möglichen Wege zur Überwindung der Krise wider. Eine der deutlichsten und zugleich grundsätzlichsten Positionen nimmt die Sudanesische Kommunistische Partei (SKP) ein. In ihrer Erklärung zum politischen Pakt der „Kräfte der Prinzipienerklärung“ entwickelt sie nicht lediglich eine Kritik an einem konkreten politischen Abkommen, sondern formuliert eine umfassende Analyse der historischen Entwicklung des sudanesischen Staates, der Ursachen des gegenwärtigen Krieges und der Bedingungen für einen demokratischen und friedlichen Wiederaufbau des Landes.


Die vorliegende Analyse untersucht die zentralen Argumentationslinien dieser Erklärung. Im Mittelpunkt stehen das Verständnis der SKP von den strukturellen Ursachen des Krieges, ihre Bewertung des politischen Paktes der „Kräfte der Prinzipienerklärung“, ihre Analyse regionaler und internationaler Einflussnahmen sowie ihre wirtschafts- und gesellschaftspolitischen Schlussfolgerungen. Ziel ist es, die politische Logik der Erklärung nachzuzeichnen und sie in den größeren Kontext der programmatischen Positionen der Sudanesischen Kommunistischen Partei einzuordnen, ohne dabei eine normative Bewertung ihrer politischen Forderungen vorzunehmen.


Von Mitgliedern der SCP in Deutschland


Eine Analyse der politischen Position der Sudanesischen Kommunistischen Partei zum politischen Pakt der „Kräfte der Prinzipienerklärung“


Kräfte der Prinzipienerklärung


/

Die Kräfte der Prinzipienerklärung Pakt sind ein politisches und zivilgesellschaftliches Bündnis, das sich im Verlauf des sudanesischen Krieges formierte. Es vereint eine Vielzahl politischer Parteien, ziviler Kräfte, Berufsverbände, Organisationen der Zivilgesellschaft sowie unabhängige nationale Persönlichkeiten. Das Bündnis wurde erstmals im Dezember 2025 öffentlich vorgestellt; seine erweiterte Charta wurde im Mai 2026 verabschiedet. Ziel des Bündnisses ist es, eine politische Vision zur Beendigung des Krieges und zum Wiederaufbau des sudanesischen Staates auf der Grundlage einer zivilen und demokratischen Ordnung vorzulegen.


Dem Bündnis gehören unter anderem die Sudanese Congress Party, die National Umma Party, die Unionist Gathering Party, die Vereinigte Nationale Unionistische Partei, die Sudanese National Alliance, die Republikanische Partei sowie mehrere nationalistische und linke Parteien an. Darüber hinaus beteiligen sich die Sudan Liberation Movement/Army unter der Führung von Abdel Wahid Mohamed al-Nur, die Sudan People’s Liberation Movement – Democratic Revolutionary Current, verschiedene Kräfte des Bündnisses „Sumoud“ sowie Berufsverbände, zivilgesellschaftliche Organisationen und unabhängige Persönlichkeiten.


Trotz der politischen Vielfalt seiner Mitglieder eint das Bündnis eine Reihe gemeinsam formulierter Grundsätze. Dazu gehören insbesondere das Ziel eines sofortigen Endes des Krieges, die Ablehnung einer militärischen Lösung, der Schutz der Zivilbevölkerung sowie die Einleitung eines politischen Prozesses, der zu einem zivilen demokratischen Übergang und zur Neugründung des sudanesischen Staates führen soll.


Gleichzeitig hat der Pakt seit seiner Veröffentlichung eine breite politische Debatte ausgelöst. Im Mittelpunkt stehen dabei Fragen nach der Zusammensetzung des Bündnisses, seinem Repräsentationsanspruch innerhalb der sudanesischen politischen Landschaft sowie die unterschiedlichen Positionen seiner Mitgliedskräfte zu grundlegenden verfassungsrechtlichen und politischen Fragen.

author: Christoph Schmon
title: New EU Court of Justice Ruling on Platform Liability Could Cause Collateral Damage to Freedom of Expression
content:
Intermediary liability laws around the world recognize that social media platforms, search engines, and other online service providers have become an integral part of our lives: they shape how we access information, communicate with others and participate in public debate, and foster innovation online. These laws generally shield platforms, to varying degrees, from legal liability for user content: the responsibility for unlawful speech should rest primarily with the speaker, not with those who merely host it.

These liability protections are not a gift for platforms. They exist so that platforms are not encouraged to proactively monitor and filter what we say online, or to remove even lawful speech simply to avoid legal risk.

This is why a recent judgment by the EU Court of Justice, Coyote System (Joined Cases C-188/24 and C-190/24), is concerning: it could deprive online platforms of liability protection because of how they organize and disseminate user content. The consequences for freedom of expression could be significant.

The European Union has long embraced a system of limited liability for online service providers. Under the e-Commerce Directive and now the Digital Services Act (DSA), platforms benefit from liability exemptions for user content. To discourage censorship, they also cannot be required to generally monitor user content or actively search for illegal activity. But that liability protection comes with qualifications: Platforms lose this benefit if they play an "active role" such that they have knowledge of, or control over, user-provided information (Recital 42 ECD, Recital 18 DSA, and case law, for example para. 113 in L’Oréal v eBay). For hosting services, providers must remove or disable content they know to be illegal. The DSA has introduced extensive due diligence obligations for platforms but left these foundational immunities intact. The message is clear: platforms bear responsibility for proper systems and processes, but generally not for users' speech.

Coyote System, however, could undermine this balance. Confronted with a case about restrictions on navigation systems that transmit information to drivers about roadside checks, the Court formulated a general test for when an intermediary ceases to be a "neutral" host and therefore loses the hosting liability exemption. In essence, the Court held that where an intermediary's algorithm goes beyond merely categorizing and indexing user information to determine, "under what conditions, how and in which order of priority" (para. 122) information is disseminated, the intermediary "controls" that information and is deprived of protection under the e-Commerce Directive.

Let's be clear: the case is not about a service that ranked or recommended user-generated content in the way social media platforms do. It is about the collection and real-time relay of user alerts about roadside checks. However, the Court's reasoning is not confined to navigation services. Recommendation algorithms determine how and in what order user content is disseminated across virtually every major online platform. Should such platforms now cease to qualify as neutral intermediaries and lose the protection of the hosting liability exemption? The answer should be no.

Control has never been understood this broadly. Nor should it be. Every hosting service provider, think of Facebook, Amazon or Bluesky, will have some control over users’ content. If that ability alone ruled the analysis, the liability exemption would become largely meaningless. Instead, the disqualifying “active role” must relate to the actual content itself, not merely the technical means by which that content is organised or disseminated.

The Court’s own case law reinforces this conclusion: In YouTube and Cyando, it examined a platform that categorises, ranks and recommends user content through algorithms, yet still proceeded on the basis that it could generally benefit from the hosting liability exemption. To be sure, the Court was mainly addressing specific knowledge of illegal content rather than the separate category of control. Even so, the underlying premise is clear: those features do not, by themselves, place a platform outside of protection. Advocate General therefore explained that what matters is the provider's "intellectual control of that content" (para 152). The relevant question is who controls the information itself, makes it their own, not who determines how it appears.

That is …

author: Unknown
title: A New World In Our Hearts - What is Mutual Aid?
content:
Occupy Sandy is an example of mutual aid: when individuals or groups voluntarily share resources and services. Community members are coming together and working to fill needs in the absence of an adequate response from government agencies and charitable organizations.

Mutual aid is one of the basic principles of anarchism. It is about working with people towards their own liberation and security, and providing concrete support to ensure that people have the power to change the conditions of their own lives.

Mutual aid is not charity. It is not about assuaging guilt, or showing off one’s own position or good fortune, nor is it about giving to those “beneath you.” It is about sharing amongst equals in different positions of need. Giving to charity, while it may have some benefit, rarely addresses the root of the problem. It doesn’t require those giving to acknowledge or question the reason for their privilege. Charity is about maintaining control; those who give the greatest dollar amounts are not interested in sharing any meaningful portion of their wealth, nor their positions of privilege in society. They may give to gain prestige, allow themselves to feel good, or any other number of reasons, but giving unlike sharing does not further equality. Mutual aid is an act that seeks to transform relationships and society for the better. Charity is something that perpetuates the status quo.

Anarchists believe that our health and freedom is bound to that of our neighbor’s irrespective of borders and other boundaries. Mutual aid is mutual because everyone is stronger, better off, and more secure if our neighbors are stronger, better off and more secure.

While of course not all of those who practice mutual aid with Occupy Sandy or through any other efforts may self-identify as anarchists, Occupy Sandy is organized in an anarchistic or horizontal structure, and is committed to many anarchist principles such as mutual aid, free association, autonomy, non-coercion, liberation, accountability, and solidarity. Ultimately anarchists believe in creating a better world free of both hierarchy and coercion.

Large authoritarian structures are good at acquiring the resources needed to address a crisis. Yet people who organize themselves freely, without unwieldy bureaucracies, are better suited to respond quickly and efficiently. We see this pattern from both the government, through FEMA, and the Red Cross’s efforts in New Orleans post Hurricane Katrina, compared with that of the anarchist inspired Common Ground Relief Organization. As we are seeing here in New York City in the aftermath of Hurricane Sandy, those well funded and staffed organizations often fall short in comparison to the ad-hoc efforts of all volunteer community powered Occupy Sandy and affiliated groups in their efforts to respond to crisis. As more people become aware of the failures of these older models of organizing, aid and relief support resources will be directed to more democratic non-hierarchical efforts.

Other examples of projects embodying mutual aid in New York City would include The Brooklyn Free Store, community dinners like Grub, and the various Food Not Bombs food shares that take place throughout the city as well as in other locations all over the world.

Get Involved! Contact mutual aid projects in your area and form your own when and where needed.

Fiz contato com funcionários e ex-funcionários públicos de todo tipo: ex-procuradores do DOJ, o Departamento de Justiça americano; advogados da SEC, o Security and Exchange Commission, ou Comissão de Valores Mobiliários. Existem até nomes que desconfio que sejam da CIA. Mas quem eu realmente quero encontrar são os agentes do FBI. 


Efeito Sonoro: ligação


Hello, my name is Natalia Viana. I’m calling for Mr. Patrick Kramer.


Trilha sonora com inspiração em filmes de espionagem


Antes de embarcar, eu tentei contato com vários deles. Nomes que conhecia apenas pelos diálogos vazados, como Patrick Kramer, um superagente, ex-marine, que chegou a ser do serviço de inteligência durante a Guerra do Golfo. Steve Moore, que atuava no consulado de São Paulo, June Drake, uma jovem agente do FBI; David Williams, que também trabalhava no consulado e é muito citado pelos membros da força tarefa da Lava Jato nos diálogos vazados. Mas existe uma agente, em especial, que eu sempre sonhei em entrevistar…


Fim da trilha


Leslie Backschies, quer dizer, Leslie Rodrigues Backshies. Rodrigues com “S” mesmo. Leslie é filha de brasileiros. Eu descobri o “Rodrigues” por acaso durante as investigações, e logo me identifiquei porque também tenho o mesmo sobrenome e, como ela, também escondo esse nome na minha assinatura. Durante anos, a única imagem que consegui de Leslie foi uma foto tirada de longe. Na imagem, dá pra ver uma mulher de meia idade, blusa rosa e calça preta, usando óculos escuros que cobre boa parte do rosto, cabelo castanho preso num rabo de cavalo e um sorriso tímido. O principal motivo do meu interesse é que Leslie se tornou uma figura muito conhecida e reconhecida pelos procuradores de Curitiba. 


Efeito sonoro: vinheta de abertura


Meu nome é Natalia Viana, sou jornalista e apresentadora da série “Confidencial: as digitais do FBI na Lava Jato”. No penúltimo episódio desta série vamos investigar quem são e qual foi a atuação de agentes do FBI e procuradores americanos durante a maior operação anticorrupção da história brasileira. 


Efeito sonoro: fim da vinheta 


Episódio 05: Os agentes


Efeito sonoro: pausa


[material de arquivo]


Reinaldo Azevedo: Desde 2016 pelo menos, a Lava Jato está operando intimamente com uma senhora chamada Leslie Rodrigues, em português mesmo esse Rodrigues, ou dona Leslie, eu não sei a pronúncia do seu nome, não sei se “Backskies” ou “Backshies”, mas B a c k s c h i e s. Ela é um medalhão do FBI, íntima, o tempo todo atuando em parceria com a Lava Jato ao arrepio do governo brasileiro. 


[Natália Viana]


Neste áudio, o jornalista Reinaldo Azevedo fala de Leslie Backschies, cuja carreira demonstra a mudança de foco do FBI. Ela inicialmente trabalhou em contraterrorismo, em 2012, mudou-se para a América do Sul, supervisionando agentes do FBI em vários países, incluindo aqueles lotados na embaixada em Brasília. A foto que mencionei prova que desde essa época ela vinha ao Brasil, o objetivo era firmar parcerias para capacitação de policiais para responder a ameaças terroristas antes da Copa de 2014. Na foto, ela está em frente a um helicóptero junto com outra agente do FBI e policiais da PM de São Paulo. Foi depois disso que a carreira de Leslie deu uma boa guinada, e ela passou a investigar casos de corrupção, e assim chegamos à Lava Jato. 


Fim da Trilha sonora 


O nome da Leslie aparece muito nos …

author: Isaac Nellist
title: India: Tens of thousands of students demand BJP education minister step down amid police violence
content:
Tens of thousands of youth and student protesters were attacked by police using tear gas and batons in India’s capital, New Delhi, on July 20, as they marched towards parliament to demand that Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign.

More than 100 students were injured in the attacks. One student, 18-year-old Anshul Dev, told Al Jazeera the government “is treating us like terrorists and criminals”.

The youth-led protests began in May after exam papers for the National Eligibility Entrance Test (NEET) leaked online, voiding exam results and forcing more than 2 million students to re-sit.

The NEET is a high-pressure nationwide exam that screens students’ eligibility for admission to undergraduate medical programs.

Protesting students called for Pradhan’s resignation over his handling of the NEET leak, and over ongoing concerns about corruption and attacks on the public education system.

This leak is only the latest in a series of leaks that have lowered trust in the education system, which many blame Pradhan and the right-wing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government for undermining.

The NEET has been the subject of longstanding controversy, including over its centralised structure, commercialised coaching culture and the immense psychological stress placed on students.

More than 12 students committed suicide after the latest exam cancellation, adding to the 93 NEET-linked student suicides across the country since 2021.

For many young people, the NEET and similar exams are critical to determining their future employment opportunities, as failure can mean lifelong poverty and disadvantage.

The protest movement gained momentum when Chief Justice Surya Kant compared unemployed youth to cockroaches and parasites, triggering widespread outrage.

In response, the satirical Cockroach Janata (People’s) Party (CJP) campaign emerged as a youth movement demanding greater transparency and accountability. The CJP campaign struck a chord with India’s “Gen Z” and has become one of the biggest expressions of dissent against Narendra Modi’s BJP government.

CJP founder Abhijit Dipke addressed a gathering at New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar — the site of an 18th century astronomical observatory — on June 6.

Dipke told the crowd that if Pradhan refused to vacate his seat, young people would refuse to vacate Jantar Mantar. Since then, a protest camp has rapidly expanded there, becoming an expression of deep anger against Modi’s attacks on youth, democratic rights and his Hindu-nationalist policies.

A wide range of student and youth groups, including the All India Students’ Association (AISA) and the Students’ Federation of India are supporting the protest movement. Several opposition politicians, celebrities and writers like Arundhati Roy have visited the camp to lend their support.

AISA president Neha Bora, alongside AISA members Manish Kumar and Aameen Amitoj, participated in a 23-day hunger strike at the camp in protest against the government. They joined renowned activist Sonam Wangchuk, who began fasting on June 28, before police forcibly admitted him to hospital over his deteriorating health, on July 18. Dozens of other students joined the hunger strike for shorter periods.

Neha, Manish and Aameen are PhD students, at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Allahabad University and Ambedkar University, respectively. While the hunger-strikers were unable to speak because of their deteriorating health, AISA representative Saiyed told AltNews they were striking because “those in power no longer believe accountability is their responsibility”.

“We are seeking Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation, the dismantling of the National Testing Agency, and the rollback of the National Education Policy 2020,” Saiyed said.

All three lost more than 10% of their body weight and were showing signs of ketosis before they ended their strike. Manish lost more than 10 kilograms and had begun bleeding from his gums, while Neha was in the worst condition, suffering from critically low blood sugar levels.

The July 20 march marked the culmination of the trio’s hunger strike. From her hospital bed, Neha said: “After the police lathi [heavy bamboo stick] charge, you have all returned after enduring injuries and tear gas, you are keeping this movement alive, my salute to all of you.

“Every stick, every drop of blood will have to be accounted for by Delhi Police … Your lathi charge will not break us, your tear gas will not break us, the …

author: Act for freedom now!
title: Ottawa: Trucks in Metro Courtyard Vandalized (Canada)
content:
Hi Metro, are you still wondering who these people are who broke into the courtyard of your distribution center in Sandy Hill? Who effortlessly drilled holes in the tires of your trucks — tweny-five to be exact — and sabotaged the braking system of six more? Who completely covered those same trucks with paint? Forcing you to wash it off quickly the next morning so you wouldn’t have to drive across town saying “Eat the Rich” and “Fuck Metro.” Oh, but wait, you couldn’t, tires were flat! As you could read on one of your trucks: no tires, no profits, right?

Well look no more, it’s us! Just Some Other Bitches Expropriating Your Shit, or as we like to call ourselves: SOBEYS. Yeah, like your rival supermarket chain in Canada. Maybe were we jealous of your reported 2025 net earnings exceeding $1 billion? Anyways, we easily found the address of one of your distribution centers and decided to make it not yours anymore. Reminding you that even when you try, you don’t have control over what you think is yours.

So go ahead, keep spending more money on security guards, maybe they’ll go on killing people in grocery stores. While you try to stop us from stealing some cheap food, we’ll slash your thousand-dollar tires. Inspired by the Robins des Ruelles in Quebec, we decided to give it a twist, hitting higher up in the chain. And if you’re wondering, yes, we can absolutely go higher.

** And for friends who might be wondering, an effective way to sabotage a semi-trailer’s braking system is to fill the two connecting lines that link the trailer to the tractor with expanding polyurethane foam. These lines look like valves; they are very accessible and are almost always located in the same place on a trailer (in the lower right corner). They allow compressed air to flow from the tractor to the trailer and transmit the signals to apply and release the brakes. The foam renders the trailer inoperable, since it becomes impossible to connect it to a tractor (and therefore to release the breaks), while posing no risk to anyone; whether it’s us doing it, the driver, or other folks on the road.

Anonymous submission to MTL Counter-info

title: Operasyonên Lûtkeya NATOyê: Yildiz Tar, Emel Memiş û xwebexşên TEMAyê serbest bûn
content:
Beriya Lûtkeya NATOyê ya 2026an Serdozgeriya Komarê ya Enqereyê lêpirsîna bi navê "operasyonên NATOyê" da dest pê kirin. 


Di çarçoveya wê lêpirsînê de rojnameger Yildiz Tar, hîndekara Zanîngeha Enqereyê ya Fakulteya Zanistên Siyasî Doç. Dr. Emel Memiş, berdevka Umut-Senê Burcu Arikan û xwebexşên TEMAyê yên ku hatibûn girtin, piştî 4 hefteyan serbest bûn.


Kesên ku hatine berdan dê darizandina wan bi awayekî negirtî berdewam bike. Tê çaverêkirin ku wê di çarçoveya dosyayê de biryarên nû yên berdanê were dayîn.


Operasyona 23ê Hezîranê û girtinên bikomî


Lêpirsînê beriya Lûtkeya NATOyê ya di 7-8ê Tîrmehê de, di serê sibaha 23ê Hezîranê de bi serdagirtina malan de dest pê kir. Di operasyonên ku bi fermana Serdozgeriyê hatin kirin de, akademîsyen, rojnamevan, parêzer û nûnerên rêxistinên jîngeh û kedê jî di nav de , bi tevahî 225 kes hatin desteserkirin. Ji wan kesan 178 kes hatin girtin, ji bo 34 kesan biryara zîndanîkirina li malê dan û tenê 6 kes serbest hatin berdan.


Serdozgeriyê ragihand ku amanca operasyonan ewe ku "deşîfrekirina çalakî û xebatên rêxistinên terorê ye". Lê di pirsiyariyan de ji gumanbaran derbarê endamtiya komele/sendîkayan, çalakiyên ku tevlî bûne û xwepêşandanên li dijî NATOyê de pirs hatin kirin.


Çalakiyên jîngeh û kedê ketin dosyayê


Di lêpirsînê de xala ku herî zêde bû sedema nîqaşê ew bû ku çalakiyên qanûnî yên jîngeh û kedê bûn mijara sûcdariyê. Ji kesên desteserkirî tevlîbûna wan a di meşên karkerên Doruk Madencilikê de û daxuyaniyên çapemeniyê yên ku tevlî bûne hatin pirsîn. Dozgeriyê îdîa kir ku dibe ku kesên desteserkirî di dema zirveyê de "çalakiyan li dar bixin", lê parêzeran diyar kirin ku dozgeriyan delîlên berbiçav esas negirtine, li gorî pêşbîniyan nirxandin kirin e.


Her wiha girtina Derhênera Weşana Giştî yê KAOS GLyê û mafparêza LGBTİ+yan Yildiz Tar, xwebexşên Weqfa TEMAyê û Doç. Dr. Memiş a bi îdîaya "endamtiya rêxistina çekdar", bû sedema bertekan û mafparêzan bi daxuyaniyan neheqiya van girtinan protesto kirin.


Beriya lûtkeyê li bajar tedbîrên awarte hatibûn girtin


Operasyon, beriya ku Walîtiya Enqereyê bi hêceta Lûtkeya NATOyê li seranserê bajarî ji bo 13 rojan hemû çalakî û xwepêşandan qedexe bikin, pêk hatin. Mafparêzan bal kişandin ser wê yekê ku ev qedexeya demdirêj a walîtiyê, mafê protestoya aştiyane bi awayekî bêpîvan binpê dike.


Walîtiya Enqereyê berê jî li 9 navçeyan ji bo ku karmend di dema Lûtkeya NATOyê de neçin ser karên xwe, betlane ragihandibû.

author: Act for freedom now!
title: Camover Communique #1: LVT Camera Tower Smashed! (Portland,USA)
content:
Early in the morning on July 1st, four Anarchists set out with hammers, a knife, and a 30′ trucker strap, to flip over and destroy a LiveView Technologies Camera Tower on Willamette Blvd in Portland. LVT, along with Flock, Axon, Ring, Waymo, Tesla, and Google, are leading the way in “AI” equipped surveillance tools, tightening the net of surveillance while finding a way to market your every move. We crept through the night and hid in the shadows for a few minutes, analyzing traffic and watching bunnies hop through the grass, indulging in their nightly play. When we felt confident, we approached the tower and found it easy to climb and wrap the rope 3/4 of the way up. Several cars passed us by, but despite being right on the shoulder, no one seemed to notice or care! We tugged and tugged with all our might, but unfortunately, 30′ did not lend enough leverage to upend the tower.

Yet all was not lost! After three minutes of trying to flip it, we gave up and instead climbed all the way to the top of the tower. This is not super easy, but can be done by anyone with a slight climbing competency. At the top we were able to smash all the cameras, while friends on the ground slashed all of the tires, and smashed all of the solar panels, leaving the tower immobile and inoperable! While smashing the cameras we noticed one of the lenses turn, either being controlled remotely from the person renting the tower, or perhaps the “AI” responding to the beautiful noise of the hammer. Whatever the case, it certainly wasn’t turning by the time we were done with it! Next time, we might consider leaving the strap at home and just climbing the tower, or getting a longer strap (maybe 45-60 feet) and more friends! Overall, we spent 5-7 minutes by the tower, and felt comfortable the entire time. It was easy to plan and easy to do! Maybe you and your friends could do it to? You can find more cameras to smash at maps.deflock.org (Including LVT camera towers!) Death to the surveillance state!

Smash every camera! Long live Anarchy! CamOver!

author: Act for freedom now!
title: Nort-sur-Erdre (Loire-Atlantique): Concrete Mixer Trucks Go Up in Smoke (France)
content:
Four concrete mixer trucks set on fire at a company near
Nantes; an investigation has been launched

During the night of Saturday, May 23, around 4:30 a.m., the gendarmerie was alerted to a fire involving concrete mixer trucks in Nort-sur-Erdre, near Nantes. “‘I heard two loud booms,’” explains a resident of the hamlet of La Verrière, who lives about one kilometer as the crow flies from Rue d’Anjou, where four concrete mixer trucks were on fire. The explosions were likely caused by bursting tires or fuel tanks on the vehicles.

This Friday, May 29, trucks blackened by flames are parked in the lot of Bétons Manufacturés de l’Erdre (BME Guimard Bétons), a family-owned business that has been manufacturing and delivering ready-mix concrete for over 40 years. “Forensic investigators have documented the scene,” states the gendarmerie, which is taking this fire very seriously, given the context of opposition against land development.

The ongoing investigation has been entrusted to the Ancenis Criminal Investigation Unit and the Nort-sur-Erdre Independent Unit.

Claim of sabotage – Spring of Local Struggles
Indymedia Nantes, May 25, 2026

On the night between Saturday and Sunday, my beloved comrades and I went out to burn four concrete mixers north of Nantes.

Let’s fight against concrete and the world it represents. Let’s destroy ecocidal industries.
It was awesome—we strongly encourage you to do the same where you live!

Despite major commitments to zero land conversion and the preservation of biodiversity, the reality is grim: France continues to pave over its agricultural and natural lands on a massive scale.
Every year, more than 24,000 hectares are still being converted to non-natural uses—equivalent to five soccer fields per hour—and this massive destruction shows no signs of slowing down. Concrete paving seals off the soil, while aggregate extraction converts farmland into artifical surfaces and destroys groundwater reserves—often irreversibly. Cement, an essential ingredient in concrete production, is responsible for 8% of global CO2 emissions and the loss of natural habitats—the leading cause of biodiversity loss.

author: Unknown
title: Hamish Kallin - Henri Lefebvre and the spatial revolution that never ends
content:
4.  Autogestion or Dictatorship

5.  An Anti-Authoritarian Theory of Space

It is widely accepted that Henri Lefebvre’s Marxism had anarchistic traits, but few have tried to specify what these traits are, or what they mean. This paper argues that Lefebvre’s work should be seen as first and foremost an anti-authoritarian theory that uses space, rather than a spatial theory. Written from a position that refuses to be either just ‘Marxist’ or just ‘anarchist’, this paper makes a claim to the possibility of a radical geography that can engage with and beyond both.

KEYWORDS anarchism, Henri Lefebvre, Marxism, radical geography, right to the city

[T]he purpose of the struggle is to go beyond democracy and beyond the democratic state, to build a society without state power.

Away with all bosses, leaders, and those apostles of language who turn words into Sacred Scripture. Avoid idolatry and value the words even of your closest friend or the wisest professor only for the truth that you find in them.

G. M. Horner (1978, p. 42) once noted that the link between Henri Lefebvre’s concept of the urban and anarchist ideas deserved ‘more than the passing acknowledgement it has so far received’. In the intervening decades, Lefebvre has become one of the foundational thinkers of critical urban studies and radical geography, but Horner’s call remains largely unanswered. Several scholars of Lefebvre have pointed out that his Marxism always seemed to contain an ambiguous proximity to anarchism, but few have really substantiated this claim. Stefan Kipfer et al. (2013, p. 126) tell us that Lefebvre’s
‘marxisme anarchisant’ (left in French because it sounds so counterintuitive in English?) was ‘sympathetic to but not synonymous with autonomism (or anarchism)’. Łukasz Stanek (2011, p. 240) notes that Lefebvre gave us an ‘anarchistic reading of Marx’. Mark Purcell (2013, p. 13) takes this further: ‘Lefebvre was very much a Marxist’, he declares. ‘He was also very much an anarchist. But he was not only one or the other, and the terms are not at all mutually exclusive’. Andy Merrifield (2011, p. 62) goes further still, suggesting that Lefebvre ‘told us long ago [that] there’s essentially no distinction between anarchism and Marxism … that precludes one practically identifying with the other’. These are intriguing assertions, doubly so because they are not put into conversation with any explicitly anarchist thinkers, nor is the implication of this confluence of isms really considered. What follows is an attempt to take these claims a little further, to try and clarify what it is specifically about Lefebvre’s work that gives it its anarchistic qualities. As I hope to show, the anarchist elements of the right to the city are crucial to its continued relevance, more so than Lefebvre was ever willing or able to comprehend.

Allow me a brief autobiographical interlude, for whilst this is not an autobiographical paper, it is one I have been chewing on for far too long, a hidden and impossible muse of sorts, held in my computer’s back pocket. I am a Marxist, and I hope this never changes. I read Marx, I take his work seriously. I use it, teach it, think with it, and write with it, and (most of) my published work reflects this. Capital, class and labour are fundamental to how I understand the world. I am also an anarchist. My teenage politicisation was anarchist (thanks largely to my dad, whose beautiful old hardback copy of The Conquest of Bread seemed to arrive from another planet), and I have never stopped reading anarchist literature, and being inspired by anarchist ideas, outside of work, behind the façade of the Marxist urban studies scholar. To some (of either tribe), that sounds foolish, as if I’m too naïve to really understand either of the traditions that I hold dear. I’m willing to admit that perhaps I am a little foolish, but I also want to try and articulate the desire for a radical geography that has space for work which draws (sincerely, respectfully, critically) from anarchism and Marxism, without pitting one against the other. You could call that position anarchist communist, libertarian Marxist, libertarian communist, some new label, or nothing at all, but there is precious little work in geography that explicitly signifies that this is where it stands. So one aim of this paper, which might seem grandiose but to me feels quite personal, is to re-frame Lefebvre as one (of many) figures who can show us this is not only possible, but …

author: Act for freedom now!
title: CALL FOR WEEK OF ACTION AGAINST THE GERMAN STATE
content:
To be clear: fascism is here. It’s time to stop moving through life and feeling like we’re seeing ghosts. Fascism is firmly rooted in the present status quo, and uprooting is our business.

On September 6th, federal state elections will be held in Sachsen-Anhalt, an AfD stronghold. Many signs are pointing towards the party gaining an absolute majority. We are tired of discussing harm reduction, strategic voting or so-called democratic practices in general. Whether the AfD will win or not, we know that current authoriatian powers all over the western world are preparing for fascism and war. And Germany plays a major role in this.
Demonstrations, human chains and petitions won’t change the system, we have to find other ways to act.

The German state is three years away from the next general elections, and people living there need to prepare for an AfD-led government. We want to talk about and practice what we need to do to destroy the workings of the state.

From an anarchist point of view, it may come as surprise that we are calling for this week of action. We don’t want to fall into blind actionism orienting itself along parliamentary politics too much. However, we have decided that now is a good moment to draw a line. There is plenty of reasons to attack the German state.

One state has gotten especially much hate over the past years, and unfortunately it is not Germany. It has been inspiring to see critical perspectives on statehood becoming more widespread in the struggle against the genocide in Palestine, yet they have largely solely focused on Israel. We believe it is important to give a lot of attention to the states we live under in our fight, there is no good state.

It is one of the most outspoken drivers of military development inside the EU, and is working on militarizing its own society at mind-numbing speeds. Questionnaires by mail are collecting information on the fighting abilities of people registered as men all around the country.

Germany has an ambition to become Europe’s biggest army … again, and has good opportunities to do so: a massive industry and an economy built on low wages, making jobs in the army and weapons industry attractive.

Civilian infrastructure and the «economy of peace» are stepping stones for the infrastructure of war. German history is a good reminder that our beloved trains are crucial for transporting troops, weapons, resources and prisoners across large distances. Companies manufacturing e.g. simple industry machines, electronics or finer parts for the automotive industry are often players in military supply chains. By now, almost every bigger city is home to some sort of military industry – from weapon production, radar equipment to drone development.

It’s time to act. Germany has been moving towards fascism over the past decade (as have many other states), and there is no doubt about it. No matter which party wins the elections on September 6th, fascists will come into even more powerful positions. They will start changing legislations and publicly denounce and attack all kinds of liberal or emancipatory projects and organisations. They will lay ground for the abuse, punishment, physical assault and prosecution of marginalized people. They will groom the police state and censorship. They have started already, yet make no mistake: After September 6th, there will be little to no chance to stop fascism by means of the state, as they will – even more so than before – be the state.

What do we do after September 6th?
We do believe in chosing our targets carefully and with care for how it may impact the lives of people who are dependent on it.

Under a fascist government, every state office and every state employee is part of it and supports it. This means that after election, all state infrastructure, even if seemingly irrelevant, is part of a fascist government and thus a legitimate target: jails, prisons, government agencies, job centers, police precincts, barracks, foreigner’s registration offices…

There are enough targets out there. We need to start choosing some, plan thouroughly, keep quiet and then go into action.

Under a facist government, fascists and nazis will feel emboldened to roam the streets and act out violently against whoever does not fit into their world view. This is something to be prepared for. By talking through what to do in case of attacks, by building care and defense networks, by re-organising an underground that has been weakend in the past …

author: Act for freedom now!
title: 10 Years on the Road – A Hug From Clandestinity
content:
From the Nowhere I hold you close to my heart and want you to know that, for the most part, I’m doing well! Unfortunately, the last few days have been a bit tough, as this anniversary kept catapulting me back to that day when I had to leave you all behind. Buried feelings resurfaced as a result of my vivid visualization of those times. It’s been 10 years… And even though time is an illusion, I keep falling back into believing in it. But now, as I write these lines to you, the past is peeling away from the old facade, and a gust of wind sweeps the future away. I am with you, whether Here or There. And there is nothing that can sever this connection.

Ten years ago, I made the decision to set out on a journey to preserve my freedom. And this freedom allowed me to explore life in all its social and cultural diversity, thereby gaining a better understanding of myself and growing from it. An endeavor that is well worth the price I’ve paid!

I can’t even express how much I’m looking forward to seeing you all again. It’s going to be wonderful. Until then, let’s stay apart, yet remain close in spirit.

Your friend and comrade from Nowhere

author: Pip Hinman
title: Brazilian socialists confirmed for Ecosocialism 2026
content:
Brazilian socialists Sabrina Fernandes and Mariana Riscali are confirmed to speak at Ecosocialism 2026.

They will join activists from Canada, India, Malaysia, Pakistan, Philippines, Singapore the United States and Australia at this year's gathering over September 11–13 at the Albion Peace Centre in Magan-djin/Brisbane.

Under the theme “Resistance, Decolonisation, Liberation”, Ecosocialism 2026 will bring together activists to discuss pathways for overcoming capitalism.

● Riscali, from the Socialist Left Movement, a current within the Socialism and Liberty Party (PSOL) in Brazil. She is a member of PSOL's National Executive Committee and executive director of the Lauro Campos and Marielle Franco Foundation.

● Debbie Kilroy, an unapologetic abolitionist whose activism and work centres on dismantling the prison-industrial complex and all forms of carceral control and exile. Kilroy is a founder of Sisters Inside, the National Network of Incarcerated and Formerly Incarcerated Women and Girls and her law firm, Kilroy & Callaghan Lawyers.

● Jodie Hall, a Wakka Wakka trans woman and Digital Campaigner at Trans Justice Project. Hall is also a member of the local action group Trans Justice Meanjin.

● Dr Elise Boyle Espinosa, whose research focuses on education and politics in conflict-affected areas, including fieldwork on the role of education in the Rojava Revolution in North and East Syria. She currently works at the School of Political Science and International Studies, University of Queensland.

● Sam Wainwright, a Socialist Alliance national co-convenor and active Stop AUKUS WA member. He was a Fremantle City Councillor and will be the Socialist Alliance WA Senate candidate at the next federal election.

● Peter Boyle, a co-founder of Rojava Solidarity – Sydney, which builds solidarity with the Kurdish-led revolution in north-east Syria. Boyle helped initiate the campaign against Aboriginal deaths in custody in the 1980s and is a Socialist Alliance National Executive member; and.

● Ben Radford, a Peruvian-Australian journalist for Green Left and trainee high school teacher. Radford was based in South America from 2023–25, reporting on grassroots struggles against extractivism, colonialism and authoritarianism.

They will join Brazilian ecosocialist Fernandes, senior Googatha elder Aunty Sue Coleman-Haseldine, Climate & Capitalism editor Ian Angus, Cuba solidarity activist Helen Yaffe, Justice for Palestine Magan-djin’s Remah Naji and Ella Teevan from the Democratic Socialists of America.

Also confirmed from the Asian region are: Kirisna Veni Singham (Socialist Party of Malaysia); Ayesha Ahmad (People’s Rights Party, Pakistan); N Sai Balaji (Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation); Khyl Ramos (Party of the Labouring Masses, the Philippines); and Rocky and Yong Feng (Singapore).

Other speakers include: Kamal Fadel from the Polisario Front (Western Sahara), Greens MP Abigail Boyd, Jews for Palestine WA’s Janet Parker and long-term LGBTIQ rights campaigner Rachel Evans.

Till skillnad från den demokratiska socialismen är för anarkismen utmärkande, att den förkastar den demokratiska principen och i allmänhet taget alla »kratier», varav det finnes många slag: autokrati (envälde); plutokrati (penningvälde); byråkrati (embetsmannavälde); aristokrati (fåvälde); demokrati (majoritetsvälde). I krati, av vad slag den vara må, ingår en föreställning om (politisk) herravälde. Ordet är nämligen bildat av det grekiska kratein, som betyder herrska. Varje lära, som i motsats till sådana, vilka göra herraväldet till ledande princip, förfäktar den personliga, enkannerligen politiska friheten, är sålunda, vad en tysk tänkare, Eugen Lũhring, skulle säga, antikratisk, vilket är raka motsatsen till övervälde.

Med besvarandet av frågan: vad bör förstås med herravälde? göra vi i det stora hela ingenting annat än avgiva en redogörelse för den politiska sidan av socialismen.

Varje herravälde förutsätter herrskare och beherrskade. Det må nu ha uppstått på vad sätt som hälst - genom arv, val, erövring, genom kallelse av någon högsta myndighet, som å sin sida kan vara en med guds nåde och de höga anornas rätt sig kallande monark, eller en representation, som genom val av det så kallade suveräna folket kommit i besittning av makten och "rätten" till herravälde: - alltid skall det finnas herrskare och beherrskare, herre och dräng. Herraväldets väsen består nu icke i ledningen som sådan, utan i ledningen medels det omedelbara tvånget. Men orättvist och förkastligt är allt tvång, som icke är ett värn mot den ursprungliga förfördelande, orättvisa makten. Nu är visserligen de herrskande personerna - byråkraterna i ordets vidsträcktaste mening - icke talrika, medan de beherrskade bilda den stora majoriteten. Det ser därför ut som om det vore minoriteten och icke tvärtom. Detta är dock ett bedrägligt sken och tillika en av demokratins, även den socialistiska demokratins fundamentala villfarelse. Det är visserligen sant att en försvinnande minoritet njuter de orättvisa frukterna av oförrätten, byråkraterna och i ännu högre grad de, som leva på räntor. Men det är majoriteten, varpå herrskarmakten stödjer sig, i regeln måste stödja sig. Det är majoriteten, varpå zarens överherrskap beror såväl som presidentens i Förenta Staterna. Det är majoriteten... som till följd av »massornas oförstånd» lyder och därigenom gör herrskarne till vad de äro - till herrskare. Den majoritet, som frivilligt lyder, d. v. s. de, som i händelse av ohörsamhet utan brutalt eller ekonomiskt tvång eller hot visa lydnad, ske i viss mening ingen egentlig orätt, även om de själva därvid äro de förorättade, (»Volenti non fit injuria», - den som vill, d. v. s. den frivilligt lydande, sker ingen orätt), vad som i regeln är fallet, alldenstund deras antal, som njuter den orättvisa fördelen, är mycket ringa.

Positiv orätt sker fastmer minoriteten, som förorättas, som tvingas till lydnad. Herraväldets verkliga väsen ligger således i de flesta fall däri, att majoriteternas representanter förorätta minoriteterna, visserligen till skada såväl för den ene som för den andre, men till uteslutande fördel för ett fåtal personer. Detta förhållande förutsätter naturligen majoriteternas hörsamhet. Men då dessa, vad redan är anmärkt, själva därvid förorättes, så kan det i sista hand blott vara massornas oförstånd; det vill säga deras slaviskhet, deras okunnighet, deras auktoritetstro och fruktan för den enskilde, som kvarhåller dem i deras beroende och gör därigenom det möjligt att uppehålla förtrycket och den ekonomiska utpressningen.

De intelligentare minoriteternas och enskilda personers våldsamma förorättande av organiserade rov- och herrsklystna makter, vilka stödja sig på majoriteter, som å sin sida lyda av oförstånd; - det har varit herraväldets väsen i alla tider, i alla land och i alla hittills varande politiska …

author: rti_admin
title: The Architecture of Trust: What Manipur Teaches us About Democracy, Conflict, and the Long Road to Peace
content:
When societies experience prolonged conflict, the most visible losses are often the easiest to count. We record the number of lives lost, the homes destroyed, the families displaced, and the schools that fall silent. These figures matter because they remind us of the scale of human suffering. Yet they reveal only part of the story. Every conflict also destroys something far less visible but infinitely more difficult to rebuild: trust.

Trust leaves no ruins for cameras to capture. It cannot be measured in relief camps or reconstructed with bricks and concrete. Yet, it is the invisible architecture upon which every democratic society depends. It is what allows citizens to believe that institutions will protect them, that laws will be applied fairly, that differences can be resolved peacefully, and that tomorrow can be planned with a reasonable expectation of safety. Like the foundation of a building, trust often goes unnoticed until it begins to crack. When that invisible architecture weakens, the consequences extend far beyond the conflict itself.

This is perhaps the most enduring lesson that Manipur offers—not only to India, but to every democracy struggling to hold together during moments of deep social division.

Much has been written about the violence that has engulfed the state since May 2023. The deaths, displacement, destruction of homes, and humanitarian suffering have rightly received national and international attention. Yet beneath these visible tragedies lies another crisis that is far less discussed: the gradual erosion of public confidence in institutions, governance, and, perhaps most painfully, in one another.

Across Manipur, the erosion of trust has manifested in different ways across regions and communities. Specifically between the valley and hilly areas like Imphal and districts such as Churachandpur, Tengnoupal, and areas including Moirang, Torbung, and Moreh, and so on, people have witnessed significant displacement, with many families forced to leave their homes and adapt to prolonged periods of insecurity. These experiences have affected communities across different parts of the state, disrupting livelihoods, education, local businesses, and long-established social relationships. Places that once facilitated regular interaction through trade, employment, education, and shared public life have become increasingly fragmented, while caution and uncertainty have gradually replaced the confidence that enables people to move freely across both social and geographical boundaries.

The tragedy, therefore, is not only that violence occurred. It is that the conflict has gradually weakened the confidence that citizens place in democratic institutions and in the relationships that make democratic life possible. Democracy survives not simply because citizens vote every few years or because constitutions define the powers of government. It survives because people believe that public institutions will act fairly, protect fundamental rights, and respond responsibly during moments of uncertainty. Elections establish governments, but trust sustains their legitimacy.

That confidence is built gradually through ordinary experiences. A child returns safely from school. A trader opens a shop expecting goods to arrive on time. A farmer transports produce to market. A citizen approaches a public office believing that the law will be applied equally. These everyday experiences rarely make headlines, yet together they create the quiet confidence upon which democratic societies depend. And conflict changes that relationship.

In moments of crisis, people begin asking different questions. Will government institutions respond fairly? Will security be provided without discrimination? Will authorities communicate honestly? Will justice be pursued consistently, regardless of identity? These questions are not merely political. They become deeply personal because they shape how citizens experience democracy in their everyday lives.

When people repeatedly perceive institutional responses as delayed, inconsistent, or insufficiently transparent, public confidence begins to erode. Whether these perceptions arise from actual administrative shortcomings, communication failures, or the extraordinary complexity of governing during conflict, the consequences remain the same. Citizens no longer judge institutions solely by their constitutional authority but by whether those institutions provide a sense of security, fairness, and …

author: Susan Price
title: Indonesia: Latest youth protests reveal failures of Prabowo’s ‘crony’ regime
content:
Green Left’s Peter Boyle spoke to Ignatius Mahendra Kusumawardhana from Perserikatan Sosialis (Socialist Union, PS), a left group in Indonesia, about the latest round of youth-led protests that kicked off in June in Jakarta.

In June this year, Indonesian young people took to the streets in protests over rising costs and fuel prices. What was the size and extent of these protests and what sparked them?

The immediate trigger was the fuel price hike of June 10, when the price of Pertamax [a widely used 92-octane gasoline sold by the state-owned energy company Pertamina] jumped from Rp12,300 to Rp16,250 per litre.

This came on top of a weakening rupiah and rising prices of staple goods.

On June 12, around 1,500 students — led by the student executive board of University of Indonesia (BEM UI) and joined by students from other campuses — marched in Jakarta.

Within a week, the actions spread to Bandung, Solo, Yogyakarta and cities in North and South Sumatra, with thousands besieging the Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat [House of Representatives, DPR] building, on June 19.

The scale of this wave of protests was smaller than the August 2025 revolt, which drew tens of thousands across the country; June was a student-led wave numbering in the thousands.

The protesters raised five demands: lower fuel and food prices, cut wasteful state spending and halt big-ticket programs like the free meals program (MBG) and rural revitalisation. Some contingents went further and demanded President Prabowo Subianto and Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resign.

On social media, the protesters used the hashtag #MenujuIndonesiaBangkrut [Towards Indonesia's Bankruptcy]. Does it demonstrate the failure of Prabowo's populist measures like the Makan Bergizi Gratis (Free Nutritious Meals, MBG) program?

The hashtag captures a real material process, not just a mood. The state budget is being drained by the ruling clique's flagship programs while the burden is shifted onto the working class: government debt now stands at Rp9,658 trillion; the rupiah is sliding toward Rp18,000 per US dollar; and in 2025, debt servicing swallowed over Rp497 trillion — more than the education or health budgets.

MBG is the sharpest illustration. In early June 2026, three top officials of the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) were arrested for misuse of MBG funds, the budget was cut from Rp335 trillion to Rp268 trillion and at least 33,000 children have suffered food poisoning.

The corruption here is not a deviation; the program functions as a mechanism of rent distribution to contractors, cronies and the military-linked network around Prabowo.

The same logic runs through the Rp400 trillion Merah Putih Village Cooperatives program, with an estimated Rp48 trillion leakage risk.

So yes, the failure is total, but it is structural, not administrative. It cannot be fixed with better management.

Are these protests similar to the round of youth protests about a year ago, in the sense of being semi-spontaneous?

Yes, in form. Like the August 2025 revolt, sparked by the DPR [MPs’] housing allowances and the police killing of the motorcycle taxi driver Affan Kurniawan, the June 2026 actions erupted semi-spontaneously, coordinated through campuses and social media rather than by any national political leadership.

The difference is the accumulation of experience: demands are now aimed directly at the budget, at concrete programs and at Prabowo-Gibran themselves.

But the weakness repeats itself at three levels: 1. The actions remain fragmented city by city, without national unification of students, workers and the urban poor into one movement with one set of demands; 2. Each explosion dissipates because it does not crystallise into durable organs of struggle; [and] 3. Most fundamentally, there is no revolutionary party rooted in the working class that can carry the lessons of one wave into the next, formulate a program and lead.

Semi-spontaneity is not a virtue to be celebrated; it is the price the movement keeps paying for the absence of that party.

What is the political significance of these repeated rounds of protest and what does it say about the Prabowo government's efforts to suppress them? How did young people react to the acid attack on human rights activist Andrie Yunus, and can we expect greater authoritarianism?

The significance of this round of protests is that repression has failed to produce demobilisation.

author: Sare Frabes
title: Comisión del EZLN viajará a Ciudad de México para encontrarse con organizaciones
content:
Tras el segundo día del encuentro denominado “Guerra contra la Humanidad. Las poblaciones y la naturaleza bajo asedio”, convocado por el Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional (EZLN), en San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas, se anuncia que una comitiva zapatista viajará a la Ciudad de México para instalarse todo el mes de diciembre y realizar una serie de encuentros con organizaciones, colectividades, pueblos originarios en resistencia y madres buscadoras.

El Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés, quien dio la noticia, advierte que México tiene que reconocer que hay “oposiciones, resistencias y rebeldías que no responden a las lógicas de liberales, conservadores, izquierdas, derechas y cosas igual de absurdas y tramposas” que buscan escapar a críticas y cuestionamientos.

Por tanto, el Insurgente Moisés, anunció que ésta visita a la Ciudad de México, tiene como objetivo provocar distintos encuentros y reuniones bajo la necesidad de un reencuentro y reconocimiento de las luchas, como las que sostienen las madres y familias que buscan a sus seres queridos en calidad de desaparecidos. Estos acercamientos servirán para amarrar acuerdos y compromisos de forma colectiva y así poder trazar estrategias para las siguientes fases de las resistencias y la lucha a nivel nacional e internacional.

El insurgente puntualizó que el EZLN hace saber a las madres que “acá, en las montañas del sureste mexicano compartimos su dolor y, sobre todo, su empeño de verdad y justicia”.

También destacó, “sentimos que tenemos que expresar personalmente nuestra admiración, nuestro cariño y nuestro respeto a los colectivos de buscadoras y buscadores”.

La última iniciativa parecida que realizó este movimiento político armado fue hace más de dos décadas, con La Otra Campaña, una iniciativa que arrancó el 1 de enero de 2006, encabezado entonces por el Subcomandante Marcos bajo el nombre de Delegado Cero. El objetivo fue escuchar a los movimientos civiles de izquierda no electoral en los 31 estados del país y el Distrito Federal.

En esta ocasión, bajo “el espíritu del común” se sugiere realizar la siguiente gira como un acuerdo con “los individuos, grupos, colectivos, movimientos y organizaciones de la Sexta México (Adherentes a la Sexta Declaración de la Selva Lacandona)”, que permitan el acercamiento con barrios, pueblos, tribus, organizaciones y movimientos.

En este evento también se pretende festejar 43 años, desde que se fundó el EZLN en su fase clandestina, ocurrido el 17 de noviembre de 1983 en la Selva Lacandona. Así mismo, el 1 de enero del 2027, se recuerdan 33 años desde el levantamiento armado público, que aconteció en 1994, cuando irrumpen con una declaración de guerra frente al Estado Mexicano quien recién había firmado el Tratado de Libre Comercio con Estados Unidos y Canadá.

“En la ciudad de México se realizará el siguiente Encuentro de Resistencias y rebeldías y el Encuentro de Artes, en diciembre de este 2026. Estaremos todo el mes de diciembre de este año 2026 y ahí, con nuestros compañeros y compañeras y compañeroas de la Sexta y de la Vida, celebraremos el aniversario del inicio de nuestro alzamiento contra el olvido el 1 de enero de 2027”, dijo el Insurgente Moisés.

El Subcomandante Moisés, precisó que los detalles de la logística se darán a conocer previo al arribo de la caravana que arribará en la Casa de los Pueblos y Comunidades Indígenas Samir Flores Soberanes, antes edificio donde despachaba el Instituto Nacional de Pueblos Indígenas y tomado, junto a otras colectividades, por la comunidad Otomí, migrante y residente en Ciudad de México.

author: Unknown
title: Zo d’Axa - Si tu m’aimes
content:
Archive Textes Auteur·e·s Sujets Mots-clés Derniers ajouts Ajouter à la bibliothèque

Applications pour appareils mobiles

Les poursuites ridicules exercées contre de vieux journalistes, l’honneur et l’argent du métier ! de scandaleuses condamnations jetant les uns à Mazas et obligeant les autres à fuir en cédant, au pied levé, la direction de leurs feuilles sont cause que, dans le monde nouveau de la presse, toutes les bonnes traditions se perdent.

Une chose honteuse vient, en effet, de se passer :

Les journaux n’ont pas craint de donner leur publicité à un fait, d’ailleurs banal ; mais que le patriotisme le plus élémentaire obligeait à passer sous silence — il s’agissait d’un soldat martyrisé par ses chefs jusqu’à ce que mort s’en suive.

Il n’aurait pas imprimé ça, lui, le Vétéran, Edmond Magnier.

Mais si l’argent reste encore un peu, si les affaires sont les affaires, celles du Lord Mayor ne suffisent pas à remplir le journal. De sorte qu’en cette période estivale, où chôme la copie, les feuilles publiques accueillent, sans scrupules, les histoires les plus scabreuses.

Les bons citoyens, les hommes sereins essaieront de se consoler en se disant que, si les théâtres étaient rouverts, nous n’aurions sans doute pas su l’édifiante malaventure de ce chasseur Chédel tué, avec d’habiles lenteurs, par son caporal aidé d’un sergent lequel était encouragé par un lieutenant — encouragé manu militari .

La publication de ce fait si peu divers de ceux qui se passent couramment n’en reste pas moins déplorable :

Un organe que le temps et la fréquence des rapports officieux ont rendu sans passion, le Petit Journal , s’exprime avec candeur.

« Chédel, épuisé, a été attaché à la crapaudine, dans une cellule où il faisait cinquante degrés de chaleur. Chédel se trouvait alors fort surexcité et dans un état de très grande fatigue. »

« Le caporal a bâillonné Chédel à trois ou quatre reprises ; d’abord avec un simple piquet de tente, puis avec un piquet et un mouchoir, et enfin avec une pierre, qui avait été placée dans la bouche. »

Allons ! messieurs de la plume professionnelle, du porte-plume tricolore, un peu de vergogne, s’il vous plaît. Croyez-vous donc avoir trouvé la réhabilitante explication en racontant qu’on a fait le nécessaire avant d’en venir à l’étouffement définitif ?

« … D’abord avec un simple piquet de tente. »

Voyons, voyons ! c’était à vous, à vous d’étouffer l’affaire. On étouffe, messieurs, que diable ! On étouffe…

Car enfin voici notre armée qui ne devait pas même être soupçonnée et qui se trouve vaincue et convaincue — vaincue à Madagascar et convaincue à Tunis… convaincue d’assassinat.

J’écris « notre armée » et ce n’est pas un mot par à-peu-près, c’est bien le mot voulu, le mot juste. C’est l’armée qui est en cause.

Oh ! certes, je ne me serais pas cru autorisé à incriminer tout un corps d’individus parce que trois ignobles brutes, aux manches maculées de galons, ont commis avec de tenaillants raffinements le plus lâche des meurtres. Le crime perpétré par les trois gradés du bataillon de discipline n’engageait, à l’origine, que leur responsabilité confuse.

Mais un conseil de guerre intervient.

L’odieux assassinat est tellement indiscutable que le commissaire du gouvernement requiert l’application de la loi. Le caporal Gally, le sergent Michel et le lieutenant Rochette ont le cynique courage de ne point nier. À peine cherchent-ils une excuse en arguant que ces choses-là sont habituelles et que d’ailleurs ils ont ponctuellement suivi — à la lettre et à l’esprit — la recommandation d’un officier supérieur leur enjoignant de « soigner » Chédel.

— Messieurs du Conseil comprendront, ajoutent-ils, le sens précis du mot « soigner ».

Et le conseil de guerre a compris. Cet arbitre qualifié de l’honneur en matière militaire s’est prononcé : un acquittement. Ce qui signifie :

— À vos postes, messieurs, et continuez…

Je n’exagère pas. On va en convenir, par force. La question posée était celle-ci :

« Les accusés avaient-ils le droit de traiter Chédel comme ils l’ont fait ? »

Et les êtres des bataillons de discipline, les pieds-de-bancs, les tortionnaires vont continuer.

La consigne plus consacrée, à présent, par une façon de jurisprudence.

Dans les sables du sud algérien, sous le ciel de métal brûlant, les petits chasseurs mauvaise-tête seront « soignés ». Sur les routes où ils cherchent des cailloux pour les casser, demain comme hier, les malheureux auront des haltes tragiques. Des képis zébrés de …

author: Unknown
title: Zo d’Axa - Les Feuilles
content:
Archive Textes Auteur·e·s Sujets Mots-clés Derniers ajouts Ajouter à la bibliothèque

Applications pour appareils mobiles

Réhabilitation civile et Exécution militaire

Félix Faure dit « Peau de Chagrin »

Considérations à propos de l’agent Rodot

Rochefort se meurt ! Rochefort est mort ! Rochefort se meurt ! Rochefort est mort !

Quelques fleurs pour une couronne

Pourquoi n’a-t-il pas tué Rotschild ?

Si nous étions « dans les huiles »

Quand on va sa route, seul, on prend à toute occasion le plaisir de dire le mot que les gens du quartier n’osent pas. Fini le souci d’édifier des voisins et la concierge. Plus de morale ! Plus de trafic ! Assez d’attrape-clientèle…

À l’argument de la masse, aux catéchismes des foules, à toutes les raisons-d’état de la collectivité, voici que s’opposent les raisons personnelles de l’Individu.

Chacun les siennes. L’isolé se gardera de prêcher une règle commune. Le réfractaire ne fait pas la place pour une doctrine. Pense toi-même ! Quel est ton cas ? Ton âge ? Ton désir ? Ta force ? As-tu besoin des béquilles que t’offrent les religions ? Si oui, retourne à ton église, désormais, par ton choix, valable. Préfères-tu, toujours disciple, le rêve des sociologues ? C’est bon, tu nous conteras tes projets pour l’an deux mille. Ou bien te sens-tu d’aplomb ? veux-tu donc vivre ? es-tu prêt ? Alors n’attends plus personne, marche à ta haine, à tes joies — aux joies des franchises totales, des risques et de la fierté.

On marche, on agit, on vise, parce qu’un instinct combatif, à la sieste nostalgique vous fait préférer la chasse. Sur la lisière du code, on braconne le gros gibier : des officiers et des juges, des daims ou des carnassiers ; on débusque aux forêts de Bondy le troupeau des politiciens ; on se plaît à prendre au collet le financier ravageur ; on relance à tous les carrefours la gent de lettres domestiquée, plumes et poils, souilleurs d’idées, terreurs de presse et de police.

Lors des querelles entre les sectes, les races ou les partis, chaque jour, au hasard des faits, des coups à porter se précisent : Demandez l’affaire Dreyfus ! ou la manière de traiter la Magistrature et l’Armée comme elles le méritent… Fêtons l’hermine et la garance ! Les démolisseurs conscients ne se spécialisèrent pas : tour à tour, selon la rencontre, ils pointèrent de droite et de gauche.

Durant le même temps, l’esprit de corps donna de jolis résultats : les magistrats, les militaires, les costumés, la livrée, tous les servants de la Société débinèrent la vieille patronne. L’office en rumeur s’aigrit. Robins, rabbins et curés, les officiants, les officiels, les officiers, les complices jonglèrent dans l’antichambre avec les objets du culte. On scandalisa les fidèles. Le doute dessilla les yeux. En quelques mois le peuple-enfant surprit qu’on lui cachait « des choses »… Maintenant la confiance est morte : les mauvais pasteurs l’ont tuée. Près de la hampe brisée du drapeau, les balances de la justice gisent comme de la ferraille parmi du bois à brûler…

C’est en vain que, la crise passée, les brocanteurs de la Patrie tenteront des raccommodages. Plus rare se fera la pratique. La bonne histoire d’une France signifiant, entre les nations, progrès, générosité, n’égarera pas tant de badauds : jamais on ne connut de tribu plus acharnée à maintenir un homme au poteau de torture.

D’ailleurs, et sans se contredire, on n’acceptera pas davantage la légende d’un Dreyfusisme, barnum de la Vérité vraie. La dame nue au miroir vit trop peu de chose dans sa glace. Elle chanta la légalité, oubliant que c’est légalement que l’on fusille les conscrits coupables d’un simple geste ; et que légalement aussi, dans nos rues, les nuits d’hiver, des hommes et des petits enfants crèvent devant les portes closes. À bas ces huis clos — les pires ! La revision qu’il faudrait, la belle dame n’en parla point.

Depuis toujours les grands mots : droit, devoir, honneur, salut-public — retentirent dans tous les clans, sous les bannières opposées. On joue des mots racoleurs. C’est une musique militaire, un chant d’église, des couplets variés de réunion publique. Les hommes qu’on n’embrigade pas font fi des mots raccrocheurs.

Sans prendre service dans les camps, ils gardent dans la mêlée la loyauté passionnée du mot juste et du coup précis. Tel état-major plus que tel autre n’a pas à compter sur eux. Ils méprisent les diplomaties, les tactiques, les réticences. Ils sont suspects : dans chaque camp, volontiers, on les traiterait en …

author: Unknown
title: anonymes - Pierre par pierre
content:
Archive Textes Auteur·e·s Sujets Mots-clés Derniers ajouts Ajouter à la bibliothèque

Applications pour appareils mobiles

C’est quoi les centres de rétention administrative ?

Donc les CRA sont des prisons ?

Peut-on accueillir tout le monde ?

Les centres de rétention sont des sortes de prisons pour enfermer les gens, principalement les étranger·es.

Pour comprendre ce que ça veut dire, il faut comprendre ce que c’est que les prisons, et ce que c’est que les étranger·es.

Après, on pourra revenir sur les nuances « sortes de » et « principalement ».

Les prisons, c’est un endroit pour punir les gens. Officiellement, c’est la plus haute punition du système pénal français. Le système pénal, c’est le système punitif mis en place et contrôlé par l’État.

L’État, c’est un instrument de pouvoir. C’est une organisation complexe qui permet à une petite classe de gens d’exercer sa domination sur de très, très grands territoires.

Ces territoires sont tellement grands que c’est impossible d’y connaître tout le monde. L’État permet donc à celles et ceux qui sont au pouvoir d’exercer leur domination sur des gens qu’iels ne connaissent pas et qu’iels n’ont même jamais croisé·es.

Le territoire d’un État ne s’arrête que lorsqu’il rencontre le territoire d’un autre État, suffisamment fort pour lui résister.

Pourquoi, les gens qui exercent leur domination au sein de l’État n’utilisent pas ce pouvoir pour dire aux gens : « Je vous ordonne de faire exactement ce que vous voulez » ?

Principalement pour deux raisons.

Premièrement, parce que dans ce cas, on ne pourrait pas savoir si les gens font ce qu’iels veulent pour obéir ou s’iels n’ont jamais eu l’intention d’obéir. Les gens qui détiennent le pouvoir ont besoin d’éprouver la réalité de ce pouvoir, et cela n’est possible qu’en forçant les gens à faire des choses qu’iels n’ont pas envie. Ce n’est que comme ça qu’on peut mesurer son pouvoir.

Deuxièmement parce que tout l’intérêt d’avoir du pouvoir, c’est de l’exercer à son profit. On appelle ça « l’exploitation ».

Les gens qui sont au pouvoir l’exercent donc à la fois pour exploiter et à la fois comme une fin en soi.

Comme les gens ne sont pas toujours d’accord pour obéir, les gens qui sont au pouvoir ont besoin de mettre en place un système coercitif, c’est le système pénal.

Le système pénal, c’est d’une part, plein de punitions et d’autre part, des tribunaux pour décider qui a désobéi et qui va faire quelle punition. Si on enlève les violences qui ne sont pas des punitions officielles – violences policières pouvant aller jusqu’à tuer ou mutiler, mise à la rue, harcèlement… – la prison est la punition la plus haute du système pénal.

Les prisons sont des bâtiments spécialement conçus pour enfermer les gens qu’on souhaite punir. Il ne s’agit pas d’enfermer les gens pendant plusieurs heures, ce qui n’est déjà pas anodin. Ça c’est plutôt le rôle des cellules de garde-à-vue [1] .

Les prisons, c’est pour enfermer, mais pour plusieurs mois. Parfois, même, pour des années.

Pour prendre la décision d’enfermer les gens en prison, c’est le tribunal qui décide.

Contrairement à une croyance largement répandue, le tribunal ne prend pas les décisions en fonction de si les gens sont méchant·es, ou pas méchant·es. (Ça c’est plutôt le Père-Noël, et de plus en plus de scientifiques remettent son existence en cause).

Le tribunal décide s’il estime que les gens ont désobéi à la volonté des gens au pouvoir.

Bien-sûr, le tribunal doit aussi avoir une certaine souplesse et faire des interprétations.

Par exemple, implicitement, la volonté de la classe au pouvoir c’est de faire fonctionner un système qui sert leurs intérêts.

Et parmi ces intérêts, il y a celui de maintenir le privilège blanc. Le tribunal a donc une certaine facilité à considérer d’office que les Noir·es ou les Arabes désobéissent à la volonté des gens au pouvoir.

Inversement, quand c’est quelqu’un·e de riche ou de proche du pouvoir qui passe au tribunal, le tribunal va plutôt considérer qu’iel n’a pas dû vraiment désobéir ou que c’est quand même pas bien grave.

Bon, ça, c’était pour expliquer la prison. Ça nous a éloigné de la question des CRA, mais c’est important de comprendre la prison pour comprendre les CRA.

L’autre élément à comprendre, c’est les étranger·es.

Au départ, un·e étranger·e, c’est quelqu’un qui n’est pas du village, mais du village d’à côté, ou d’un peu plus loin.

Avant la première guerre mondiale, il n’y avait pas, en France, de définition juridique …
